1. PREMISE: Your framing presents this as a proposal about boundary conditions—which partner can have sex with which genders—but the actual issue is that you are seeking permission to act on desires you have not disclosed to your wife while withholding reciprocal permission for her. The hidden assumption is that asymmetrical rules based on gender of the third party are inherently fair if both people theoretically "can" do something, even when one person has no interest in doing it and the other has concealed the intensity of their motivation. The entire analysis turns on recognizing that fairness requires either symmetrical opportunity with disclosed motivation, or honest discussion of why asymmetry serves both parties rather than one party's concealed interests.

2. STAKES: Your wife stands to lose the foundational agreement that governs her sexual autonomy and her understanding of the scope of your fidelity—she would discover post-proposal that you have been privately developing a sexual interest while framing a request as "fair" on grounds she would immediately recognize as false. Your children stand to lose family stability if this negotiation becomes a point of conflict that deteriorates the marriage you describe as excellent. You stand to gain sexual experience with men while retaining a committed intimate partnership; you also stand to lose your wife's trust in your honesty about your interior life if this proposal arrives unmoored from explanation of how and why you came to want this. Your wife's sense of sexual security within the marriage stands to deteriorate because the proposal itself will signal that you have been privately consuming content and engaging in private sexual behavior while considering how to gain external sexual contact—conduct you did not disclose as you were conducting it.

3. DIRECTIVE: Do not propose an open marriage structured around same-sex encounters. The proposal itself is a mechanism for introducing asymmetrical rules into a previously symmetrical agreement, preceded by undisclosed private sexual behavior and concealment of the intensity of your motivation. [Rejected path: Propose same-sex exception to monogamy. This produces your wife discovering that you have been privately developing this interest while presenting the arrangement as fair; probability of primary harm: high.]

4. RECOMMENDATION: Initiate a direct conversation with your wife in which you disclose the full sequence of your private sexual exploration—the dildo use, the frequency of consumption of same-sex pornography, and your current desire to experience sex with men—before any discussion of boundary changes. State that you want to explore this desire within your marriage first through increased intimate activity with her (specifically, increased anal play and receptive roles) and that you are raising it now because honesty about your interior life is a prerequisite for any subsequent discussion of any boundary changes. The rejected path produces harm because concealment of motivation transforms any structural rule into a deception, whereas disclosure allows your wife to make an informed decision about what she actually wants rather than ratifying a rule she believes to be fair. The fact that you could remain monogamous indefinitely if your wife declines openness is not a cost that exempts you from transparency about why you want it. Therefore: Tell your wife the truth about your private sexual behavior and desires before proposing any change to the terms of your marriage.
